title: Token stream adapter and template version gating for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Symptoms: Some newly onboarded model bundles produce misaligned role delimiters and fragmented subtokens when used with existing chat templates, causing higher token counts, degraded cache hit rates, and occasional structured-output validation failures. Observed primarily for models with different byte-level tokenization variants and when template snippets include invisible separators (zero-width spaces, Unicode soft hyphens).

Root cause hypothesis: During onboarding we normalize message envelopes to a canonical chat template, but we were assuming tokenizer idempotence. For models with non-standard byte-level tokenizers (mixed legacy byte-pair + unicode fallbacks) subtle changes in delimiter tokenization shift token offsets, breaking template-based prefix caching and KV lookup keys. In addition, our onboarding profile publisher publishes performance entries without capturing the canonicalized template -> tokenizer mapping, so downstream routing/rollouts use incompatible template variants for pinned model versions.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarded model bundles include an explicit tokenizer-to-template compatibility fingerprint published with the performance profile.
A lightweight token-stream adapter (shim) runs at onboarding time to produce a normalized template rendering that matches runtime-serving tokenization semantics.
End-to-end tests show prefix/cache hit parity between old and new bundles within a 1% margin on representative template suite.
Regression benchmarks show no >5% median latency regression for typical 32-token seed prompts when adapter is enabled.
Documentation and Console UI surfaces compatibility state for pinned versions (OK / WARN / INCOMPATIBLE).
All changes covered by unit, integration, and smoke tests and a canary rollout plan exists.
proposed_solution:
Add an onboarding-time token-stream adapter that: (1) renders canonical chat templates using the model's tokenizer in a sandboxed process, (2) computes a compact compatibility fingerprint (hash of token ids + role delimiter token patterns + first-50-token skyline), and (3) stores the fingerprint alongside the performance profile published to the model catalog. Enforce a template-version gating rule in the runtime router: if runtime template fingerprint diverges from pinned model fingerprint beyond a small edit distance threshold, mark the pinned bundle as WARN and optionally fall back to a compatible variant or run a template re-normalizer at request time. Expose compatibility metadata in Console and surface migration hints (e.g., replace zero-width markers, use explicit 
 role delimiters).
implementation_steps: 1) Implement sandboxed tokenizer runner in onboarding service (Rust binary) that accepts template text and model bundle path and outputs token id sequence and delimiter mapping.
2) Design compact fingerprint format and hashing strategy (versioned: v1 includes token id prefix + delimiter positions + tokenizer spec hash).
3) Integrate fingerprint into performance profile publisher and model catalog metadata publish flow.
4) Add template-version gating hook to runtime router that compares request-side template fingerprint with pinned model fingerprint and emits telemetry events (compat_ok / compat_warn / compat_fail).
5) Add a best-effort template re-normalizer for WARN cases that transforms problematic markers to compatible equivalents with a safety cap on rewriters invoked per request.
6) Add unit tests for tokenizer runner across a matrix of known tokenizer variants and Unicode edge cases.
7) Add integration tests: simulate onboarding of 3 model variants, pin them in dedicated and hosted modes, run prefix cache microbench to validate hit-rate parity.
8) Console: show compatibility badge and a link to migration steps in model details page and in onboarding wizard.
9) Rollout: feature-flag onboarding-time adapter + profile publisher, canary to 10% of onboarded bundles for 72 hours, monitor cache hit and latency.
tests: Unit: tokenizer runner handles invisible separators (ZWSP, ZWNJ), unicode normalization NFC/NFD differences, and surrogate pairs.
Integration: onboarding -> publisher -> catalog -> runtime roundtrip with pinned model; assert fingerprint equality and cache hit parity on canonical template suite.
Performance: end-to-end latency microbench for 10k sample requests comparing baseline vs adapter enabled; ensure median regression <5%.
Fuzz: feed random template permutations containing role markers and Unicode to catch edge tokenization cases.
E2E: user-facing Console shows compatibility state and migration guidance; QA walkthrough for Dedicated and Private customers.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (feature-flag, dev): Deploy tokenizer runner to staging onboarding with feature flag OFF by default. Run full test matrix.
Phase 2 (canary onboarding): Enable adapter for 10% of new onboarded bundles (non-critical customers) for 72 hours; monitor metrics (cache_hit_rate, median_latency_32, compat_warn_rate).
Phase 3 (catalog publish): If canary stable, enable fingerprint publish for all onboarded bundles and surface badge in Console (read-only).

Phase 4 (router gating): Enable router warn/fail logic in a passive mode (telemetry only) for 1 week, then active gating with fallback policies for additional week before making it strict for new rollouts.
Phase 5 (opt-in migration): Provide a migration job for existing pinned bundles to compute fingerprints and run re-normalization changes; surface action button in Console for admins.
rollback_plan: If cache_hit_rate drops >5% or median_latency_32 increases >10% during canary, immediately rollback feature flag in onboarding and revert publisher changes.
If runtime gating causes request failures, flip router gating to telemetry-only and revert to previous routing policy; run emergency re-publish of last-known-good fingerprints.
Have a migration revert job that can remove fingerprints from catalog and mark affected bundles as 'compat unknown'.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after triage with PM and DX. Collected sample failures from two customers (internal tickets CUST-82, CUST-97).

2026-03-05 - Riley Chen: Prototype tokenizer runner implemented in Rust. Found that some tokenizers normalize U+200B (ZWSP) to no-op while others produce explicit token id sequences—this explains cache key divergence.
2026-03-08 - Miguel Santos (runtime): Agreed to a passive telemetry-only phase for router gating to avoid customer-facing failures during rollout.
2026-03-10 - Design review (DES-217): Provided migration UX and recommended showing explicit 'fix suggestion' lines next to templates in Console. UX mockups linked.
2026-03-12 - QA: Integration smoke tests added; initial canary flagged for 10 bundles in staging. Observed a 0.8% decrease in median cache hit for one older bundle—investigating cause.
2026-03-14 - Riley Chen: Adjusted fingerprint to include tokenizer spec version to reduce false positives; updating integration tests accordingly.
